Why My Bill

The problem · Page 2 of 10

A bill says what you owe. Never why it changed.

For UK households with electricity, gas and water bills: the person who opens this month’s bill, sees it’s £32 higher than last month, and wonders why.

Usually mundane

  • A longer billing period
  • A colder month
  • A price change
  • An estimated reading

Sometimes it matters

  • A leak
  • A new appliance
  • A switch from gas to a heat pump

Each cause needs a different response, and a guess can cost money: a leak left running, or a tariff switch over a bill that was only longer.

Why My Bill

Zetaris · Page 6 of 10

Zetaris is the only way the agents see data

5 queries

behind the January gas answer, each read-only and hashed with SHA-256.

Six sources

Supplier bills and meter readings, the water company’s bills and charges (three formats), and two live public APIs: Octopus tariffs and Open-Meteo weather

Tables and views

Nine Lightning REST tables, cached; four SchemaStore views put them in one shape: pence to pounds, litres to m³, UTC to UK dates

Read-only

One SELECT per agent tool, checked against the bill’s signed contract; every read is evidence with its SQL and SHA-256

Live data in

A bill the household adds is saved in its supplier’s format; UNCACHE and CACHE TABLE refresh it in about a second

Why My Bill

Meterless · Page 7 of 10

Meterless at every step

18 of 18

model calls in the January gas answer went through Nightshift, each with a receipt.

Nightshift

The gateway for every Nemotron call. The NVIDIA key lives there, and each call’s receipt is on the page.

Scout Intent

Published as a spec with no code, so we built it: the guard, intent routing and a signed, expiring contract per bill. Meterless’s own harness passes it.

World Model

The case file: bills and causes as entities, every finding and review a fact with provenance.

Markovian

Runs the orchestrator’s review rounds, carrying state from one round to the next.

H-MEM

Household notes, saved findings, feedback that changes what is recalled, and an audit trail on the page.

Why My Bill

What was unique · Page 8 of 10

Guarantees, not plumbing

58/58

answer-key checks, in both full runs: on the local files and through Zetaris.

Zetaris is the boundary, not a dump

The agents never see a file. Every number in an answer traces to a read-only query and a hash of its rows.

A signed contract scopes every agent

Scout signs one per bill, naming the bills and data allowed; the agent loop refuses any tool it doesn’t grant.

Memory the household controls

A “No” on an answer flags the notes it used, and recall leaves them out until kept. Every change is in H-MEM’s audit, on the page.

We tested the platform as we built

Nightshift injected earlier answers into prompts: now a fresh scope per call, 0 of 132 injected. NVIDIA rejected bursts: calls are paced, 68 rejections to none.
